subject: math
title: Skip Counting by 5s, 10s and 100s
seo_title: Grade 2 Skip Counting Worksheets: Count by 5s, 10s and 100s Within 1000
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 skip counting worksheets: count by 5s with hands, nickels and tally marks, count by 10s and 100s from any number, count on and back across a hundred, and solve simple stories. 100 practice questions with simple answers explained.
key_big: Skip counting is jumping by the same number each time.
key_sub: Count by 10s and only the tens digit changes: 37, 47, 57. Count by 100s and only the hundreds digit changes: 240, 340, 440. After 199 comes 200.
body_html:
Skip counting means jumping by the same number

When you skip count, you do not say every number. You jump by the same amount each time: by 5s, by 10s or by 100s. It is a fast way to count many things.

Count byExampleWhat changes
5s5, 10, 15, 20, 25The last digit goes 5, 0, 5, 0
10s37, 47, 57, 67Only the tens digit
100s240, 340, 440, 540Only the hundreds digit

Count by 5s

Use hands, nickels or tally marks. Each one is a group of 5.

Count by 10s from any number

You can start at any number, not only at 10. The ones digit stays the same.

On a hundred chart, the number just below is 10 more.

Count by 100s

Count by 100s: 108, 208, 308, ☐

Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. The 08 stays the same.

Answer: 408

Crossing a hundred

10 ones make a ten, and 10 tens make a hundred. So after 199 comes 200, and after 390 (counting by 10s) comes 400.

Count byAcross a hundred
1s197, 198, 199, 200, 201
10s372, 382, 392, 402, 412
1s, back402, 401, 400, 399, 398

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Changing the ones digit when counting by 10s: 37, 47, 58Keep the ones digit: 37, 47, 57
Changing the tens digit when counting by 100s: 240, 340, 450Only the hundreds change: 440
Writing 1100 or 1000 after 199199 + 1 = 200
Writing 3102 after 392 when counting by 10s10 tens make a hundred: 402
Counting tally groups as 4Each group has 5 marks: 4 sticks and a slash

faq.q: What is skip counting in 2nd grade?
faq.a: Skip counting is counting by the same number each time instead of by 1s. Grade 2 students skip count by 5s, 10s and 100s within 1000, for example 240, 340, 440, 540.

faq.q: How do you teach skip counting by 5s?
faq.a: Use things that come in fives: fingers on a hand, nickels and tally marks. Count each group by 5s (5, 10, 15, 20) and point out that the last digit always goes 5, 0, 5, 0.

faq.q: How do you skip count by 10s from a number that does not end in 0?
faq.a: Keep the ones digit the same and add 1 to the tens digit each time: 37, 47, 57, 67. A hundred chart helps, because each number directly below is 10 more.

faq.q: Why does my child write 1100 after 199?
faq.a: They add 1 to the 99 and write 100 after the 1. Show that 9 ones and 1 more make a ten, and 9 tens and 1 more ten make a hundred, so 199 + 1 = 200.

items.q: Count by 5s. How many fingers are there in all?
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count by 5s, one hand at a time: 5, 10, 15. There are 15 fingers.

items.q: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 15 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Each nickel is worth 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20¢.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Each group has 4 sticks and 1 slash. That is 5 marks. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 marks.

items.q: Count by 5s. How many fingers are there in all?
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count by 5s, one hand at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Count by 5s: 35, 40, 45, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 45 + 5 = 50. 46 is counting by 1s.

items.q: Each nickel is worth 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25¢.

items.q: When you count by 5s from 0, what is the last digit of each number?
items.e: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 … The last digit goes 0, 5, 0, 5. So it is always 0 or 5.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Each group has 4 sticks and 1 slash. That is 5 marks. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. There are 25 marks.

items.q: Count by 5s: 20, 25, ☐, 35. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number comes after 25 and before 35. 25 + 5 = 30, and 30 + 5 = 35.

items.q: Count by 5s. How many fingers are there in all?
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count by 5s, one hand at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. There are 30 fingers.

items.q: Each nickel is worth 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. That is 35¢.

items.q: Count back by 5s: 60, 55, 50, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back, each number is 5 less. 50 − 5 = 45. 49 is counting back by 1s.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Each group has 4 sticks and 1 slash. That is 5 marks. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. There are 35 marks.

items.q: Count by 5s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: When you count by 5s from 0, every number ends in 0 or 5. 45 ends in 5. 42, 54 and 48 do not.

items.q: Count by 5s: 85, 90, 95, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 95 + 5 = 100. After 95 comes 100, not 910. 9 tens and 1 more ten make 1 hundred.

items.q: Count by 5s. How many fingers are there in all?
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count by 5s, one hand at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. There are 40 fingers.

items.q: Each nickel is worth 5¢. How much money is this?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. That is 45¢.

items.q: How many tally marks are there?
items.e: Count the groups by 5s: 5, 10, 15. Then count on by 1s for the 2 single sticks: 16, 17. There are 17 marks.

items.q: Count by 5s: 110, 115, 120, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 120 + 5 = 125. The hundreds digit stays 1.

items.q: Count by 10s: 37, 47, 57, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 7. 57 + 10 = 67.

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: In a hundred chart, each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 34. 34 + 10 = 44.

items.q: Count by 10s: 14, 24, 34, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 4. 34 + 10 = 44.

items.q: Start at 26. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +10. Count by 10s from 26: 36, 46, 56. You land on 56.

items.q: Count by 10s: 37, 47, 57. Which digit changes each time?
items.e: 37, 47, 57: the 7 stays the same. The 3, 4, 5 go up by 1. That is the tens digit.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 93, 83, 73, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 10s, each number is 10 less. The ones digit stays 3. 73 − 10 = 63.

items.q: Count by 10s: 52, 62, 72, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 2. 72 + 10 = 82.

items.q: Count by 10s: 46, ☐, 66, 76. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 10 more than 46. 46 + 10 = 56. Then 56 + 10 = 66.

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: In a hundred chart, each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 48. 48 + 10 = 58.

items.q: Start at 148. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +10. Count by 10s from 148: 158, 168, 178, 188. You land on 188.

items.q: Count by 10s: 125, 135, 145, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 5. 145 + 10 = 155.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 486, 476, 466, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 10s, each number is 10 less. The ones digit stays 6. 466 − 10 = 456.

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: In a hundred chart, each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 174. 174 + 10 = 184.

items.q: Start at 84. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is back 10. Count back by 10s: 74, 64, 54. You land on 54.

items.q: Count by 10s: 263, 273, 283, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 3. 283 + 10 = 293.

items.q: Count by 10s: 305, ☐, 325, 335. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 10 more than 305. 305 + 10 = 315. Then 315 + 10 = 325.

items.q: Start at 365. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +10. Count by 10s from 365: 375, 385, 395. You land on 395.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 271, 261, 251, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 10s, each number is 10 less. The ones digit stays 1. 251 − 10 = 241.

items.q: This is part of a hundred chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: In a hundred chart, each row is 10 more than the row above. The number above the ? is 526. 526 + 10 = 536.

items.q: Count by 10s: 418, 428, 438, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up by 1. The ones digit stays 8. 438 + 10 = 448.

items.q: Count by 100s: 240, 340, 440, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 440 + 100 = 540.

items.q: Start at 150. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +100. Count by 100s from 150: 250, 350, 450. You land on 450.

items.q: Count by 100s: 108, 208, 308, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 308 + 100 = 408.

items.q: Count by 100s: 264, 364, 464. Which digit changes each time?
items.e: The 64 stays the same. The 2, 3, 4 go up by 1. That is the hundreds digit.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 975, 875, 775, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 100s, the hundreds digit goes down by 1. 775 − 100 = 675.

items.q: Count by 100s: 315, 415, 515, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 515 + 100 = 615.

items.q: Count by 100s: 163, ☐, 363, 463. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 100 more than 163. 163 + 100 = 263.

items.q: Which list counts by 100s?
items.e: Counting by 100s, only the hundreds digit goes up by 1: 312, 412, 512. 312, 322, 332 counts by 10s.

items.q: Count by 100s: 52, 152, 252, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 252 + 100 = 352.

items.q: Start at 230. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +100. Count by 100s from 230: 330, 430, 530, 630. You land on 630.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 610, 510, 410, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 100s, the hundreds digit goes down by 1. 410 − 100 = 310.

items.q: Start at 425. Count on by 100s three times. Where do you stop?
items.e: Count by 100s three times: 525, 625, 725. Do not count 425 as one of the three.

items.q: Count by 100s: 436, 536, 636, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 636 + 100 = 736.

items.q: Count by 100s: 507, ☐, 707, 807. What number is missing?
items.e: The missing number is 100 more than 507. 507 + 100 = 607.

items.q: Count by 100s: 700, 800, 900, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 900 + 100 = 1000. 9 hundreds and 1 more hundred make 10 hundreds. 10 hundreds is one thousand.

items.q: Start at 920. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is back 100. Count back by 100s: 820, 720, 620. You land on 620.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 999, 899, 799, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Counting back by 100s, the hundreds digit goes down by 1. 799 − 100 = 699.

items.q: Start at 680. Count back by 100s two times. Where do you stop?
items.e: Count back by 100s two times: 580, 480.

items.q: Count by 100s: 199, 299, 399, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 399 + 100 = 499.

items.q: Sofia starts at 300 and counts by 100s to 800. How many jumps does she make?
items.e: Count the jumps: 400, 500, 600, 700, 800. That is 5 jumps. Do not count 300, because that is where she starts.

sets.title: Count on and back across a hundred

items.q: Count on: 197, 198, 199, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 199 + 1 = 200. 9 ones and 1 more make a ten. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a hundred. So 199 becomes 200, not 1100.

items.q: Each tick is 1 more. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count on by 1s from 196: 197, 198, 199, 200. After 199 comes 200.

items.q: Count back: 402, 401, 400, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 400 − 1 = 399. Just before 400 is 399. The hundreds go down to 3, and the tens and ones become 9.

items.q: Count on: 348, 349, ☐, 351. What number is missing?
items.e: 349 + 1 = 350. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. Then 350 + 1 = 351.

items.q: Count on: 298, 299, ☐, 301. What number is missing?
items.e: 299 + 1 = 300. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a new hundred. Then 300 + 1 = 301.

items.q: What number comes just before 600?
items.e: Count back 1 from 600: 599. 601 comes just after 600.

items.q: Each tick is 1 more. What number goes at the ?
items.e: Count on by 1s from 397: 398, 399, 400, 401, 402. Count each jump, not the first tick.

items.q: Count on: 597, 598, 599, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 599 + 1 = 600. The ones and tens become 0, and the hundreds go up by 1.

items.q: Count back: 703, 702, 701, 700, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 700 − 1 = 699. Just before a hundred, the tens and ones are 9.

items.q: Which list counts on by 1s?
items.e: After 199 comes 200, then 201. The right list is 198, 199, 200, 201.

items.q: Count by 10s: 670, 680, 690, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 690 + 10 = 700. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a new hundred. So 6 hundreds become 7 hundreds.

items.q: Count back by 10s: 520, 510, 500, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 500 − 10 = 490. Going back past 500, the hundreds go down to 4, and the tens become 9.

items.q: Each tick is 1 more. What number goes at the ?
Lily starts at 597 and counts on 6 more. Where does she stop?
items.e: Count 6 numbers after 597: 598, 599, 600, 601, 602, 603. Do not count 597.

items.q: Count by 10s: 372, 382, 392, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 392 + 10 = 402. 9 tens and 1 more ten make a new hundred, and the ones stay 2.

items.q: Count back by 5s: 315, 310, 305, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 305 − 5 = 300. Each number is 5 less.

items.q: Each tick is 1 more. What number goes at the ?
What number comes just after 999?
items.e: 999 + 1 = 1000. 9 hundreds and 1 more hundred make 10 hundreds, which is one thousand.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 350, 250, 150, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: 150 − 100 = 50. Take away 1 hundred, and there are no hundreds left. 5 tens are still there.

items.q: Count back: 1000, 999, 998, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 less. 998 − 1 = 997.

items.q: Luis counts the fingers on 7 hands. Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers are there?
items.e: Count by 5s 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. There are 35 fingers.

items.q: Ruby has 6 nickels. A nickel is worth 5¢. How much money does she have?
items.e: Count by 5s 6 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 30¢.

items.q: Sam reads 10 pages each day. How many pages does he read in 8 days?
items.e: Count by 10s 8 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. That is 80 pages.

items.q: A box has 10 crayons. Ben has 9 boxes. How many crayons does he have?
items.e: Count by 10s 9 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. He has 90 crayons.

items.q: Grace jumps by 5s on a number path. She starts at 0. Where is she after 9 jumps?
What is the rule? 345, 355, 365, 375
items.e: Only the tens digit goes up by 1 each time: 345, 355, 365, 375. The rule is count by 10s.

items.q: Ava counts down for a rocket by 10s: 100, 90, 80 … What does she say after 40?
items.e: Counting back by 10s, each number is 10 less. 40 − 10 = 30.

items.q: A store has 6 boxes. Each box has 100 pencils. How many pencils are there?
items.e: Count by 100s 6 times: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600. There are 600 pencils.

items.q: You count by 5s from 5. Which number do you NOT say?
items.e: Counting by 5s from 5, every number ends in 0 or 5. 40, 55 and 70 do. 62 ends in 2, so you do not say it.

items.q: Zoe counts her nickels: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. How many nickels does she have?
items.e: She says one number for each nickel. There are 7 numbers, so she has 7 nickels. 35¢ is how much they are worth.

items.q: Kai has 120 stamps. He gets 10 more stamps each week. How many stamps does he have after 4 weeks?
items.e: Start at 120 and count by 10s 4 times: 130, 140, 150, 160. He has 160 stamps.

items.q: What is the rule? 520, 515, 510, 505
items.e: The numbers get smaller by 5 each time: 520, 515, 510, 505. The rule is count back by 5s.

items.q: Owen counts by 10s from 7: 7, 17, 27 … Which number will he say?
items.e: Counting by 10s from 7, the ones digit is always 7: 7, 17, 27, 37, 47, 57.

items.q: Nora has 900 points in a game. She loses 100 points each turn. How many points does she have after 3 turns?
items.e: Start at 900 and count back by 100s 3 times: 800, 700, 600. She has 600 points.

items.q: Omar has 250 points. He gets 100 points for each level. How many points does he have after 3 more levels?
items.e: Start at 250 and count by 100s 3 times: 350, 450, 550. He has 550 points.

items.q: What is the rule? 128, 228, 328, 428
items.e: Only the hundreds digit goes up by 1 each time. The rule is count by 100s.

items.q: Eli has 3 dimes and 2 nickels. How much money is that?
items.e: Count the dimes by 10s: 10, 20, 30. Then count the nickels by 5s: 35, 40. That is 40¢.

items.q: The class voted with tally marks. How many votes are there?
items.e: Count the 6 groups by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Then count on 3 single sticks: 31, 32, 33. There are 33 votes.

items.q: A pack has 10 stickers. Leo has 4 packs and 5 more stickers. How many stickers does he have?
items.e: Count the packs by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. Then count on 5 by 1s: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45. He has 45 stickers.

items.q: A bag has 100 beads. Mia has 3 bags and 2 strings of 10 beads. How many beads does she have?
items.e: Count the bags by 100s: 100, 200, 300. Then count the strings by 10s: 310, 320. She has 320 beads.
